blocks.text: ZeRO-1, the first stage of the Zero Redundancy Optimizer family, shards optimizer state across participating devices rather than replicating a full copy on every device, directly targeting the optimizer state memory consumer covered in the earlier VRAM Management topic while leaving model weights and gradients fully replicated.

This topic covers ZeRO-1 specifically as the foundation for the progressively more aggressive ZeRO-2 and ZeRO-3 stages covered in the next two topics of this module, each sharding one additional VRAM consumer.
1. What ZeRO Stands For

blocks.alt: Zero Redundancy Optimizer gives ZeRO its name

blocks.text: ZeRO stands for Zero Redundancy Optimizer, a name reflecting its core goal, eliminating the redundant duplication of data across devices that standard data parallelism, covered earlier in this module, involves, starting specifically with optimizer state in this first stage.
2. ZeRO Stage 1, What Gets Sharded

blocks.alt: Model weights stay replicated while optimizer state gets sharded in ZeRO-1

blocks.text: ZeRO-1 specifically shards optimizer state, covered in the Optimizer States topic, splitting it across devices so each device holds only a portion, while model weights and gradients remain fully replicated on every device, exactly as they would under standard data parallelism.
3. Optimizer State Sharding Specifically

blocks.alt: Device one holds optimizer state shard A while device two holds shard B

blocks.text: Since optimizer state, particularly for Adam and AdamW covered in the earlier Optimizers module, can require roughly twice the memory of the model weights themselves, sharding just this one consumer across devices already delivers a meaningful memory reduction without touching weights or gradients at all.

# A conceptual sketch of ZeRO-1 optimizer state sharding
device_optimizer_shard = optimizer_state[device_rank::num_devices]
# Each device only stores and updates its own shard of optimizer state

blocks.text: 4. ZeRO-1 Memory Savings

blocks.alt: Unsharded, full optimizer state per device is compared against ZeRO-1 sharded state split across devices

blocks.text: The memory savings from ZeRO-1 scale with the number of participating devices, more devices means each one holds a smaller shard of the total optimizer state, directly reducing the largest single VRAM consumer for optimizers like Adam covered in the earlier Optimizer States topic.

blocks.text: 5. ZeRO-1 Communication Overhead

blocks.alt: The relevant shard gets gathered when needed, then the update gets applied

blocks.text: Because each device only holds a portion of the optimizer state, some additional coordination is needed to correctly apply weight updates using the gathered, combined state, introducing communication overhead beyond what standard data parallelism requires, though generally modest compared to the memory savings gained.
6. ZeRO-1 vs Standard Data Parallelism

blocks.alt: Standard data parallelism is compared against ZeRO-1

blocks.text: ZeRO-1 keeps the same core data parallel structure covered in the earlier Data Parallelism topic, splitting the batch across devices, but adds optimizer state sharding on top, making it a comparatively low complexity first step up from standard data parallelism toward the more aggressive memory savings ZeRO-2 and ZeRO-3 provide.
7. ZeRO-1 as the Foundation for Later Stages

blocks.alt: ZeRO-1 forms the foundation that ZeRO-2 and ZeRO-3 build on

blocks.text: ZeRO-2, covered in the next topic of this module, builds directly on ZeRO-1 by additionally sharding gradients, and ZeRO-3 goes further still by sharding model weights themselves, each stage a progressively more aggressive extension of this same core sharding idea.

blocks.title: Understanding ZeRO-1 clearly makes the next two topics much easier
blocks.content: Since ZeRO-2 and ZeRO-3 are direct extensions of ZeRO-1, adding one more sharded consumer at each stage, a solid grasp of this first stage is the foundation the rest of this progression builds on.

blocks.text: 8. When ZeRO-1 Alone Is Enough

ZeRO-1 alone is often enough when optimizer state was the primary memory bottleneck, and model weights and gradients already fit comfortably replicated across devices, a common situation for models of moderate size trained with Adam or AdamW.
9. ZeRO-1 in Practice

ZeRO-1 is typically enabled through a simple configuration setting within DeepSpeed, covered in the previous topic, or another supporting framework, requiring no manual implementation of the underlying sharding and gathering logic.
Worked Example

A team fine-tuning with AdamW across four devices finds their optimizer state, roughly twice the size of their model weights, is the single largest memory consumer in their training setup, even though the weights and gradients themselves fit comfortably.

Enabling ZeRO-1 shards that optimizer state across their four devices, each holding only a quarter of it, freeing up substantial memory without needing to touch how weights or gradients are handled at all, resolving their specific memory bottleneck with a comparatively simple configuration change.
Common Mistakes

items: Jumping straight to ZeRO-3 when ZeRO-1 alone would have addressed the actual optimizer state bottleneck
Not recognizing optimizer state, rather than weights, as the actual memory bottleneck before choosing a ZeRO stage
Assuming ZeRO-1 shards model weights, when it specifically shards optimizer state while leaving weights replicated
Overlooking the communication overhead ZeRO-1 introduces when evaluating whether it fits a specific training setup

blocks.text: Practice

For a training setup using AdamW across a number of devices you choose, calculate how much optimizer state memory each device would need under ZeRO-1 compared to standard data parallelism, where every device holds the full state.
Key Takeaway

ZeRO-1 shards optimizer state across participating devices while keeping model weights and gradients fully replicated, directly addressing the often substantial optimizer state memory consumer covered in the earlier Optimizer States topic, and it serves as the foundation the more aggressive ZeRO-2 and ZeRO-3 stages build on by sharding additional consumers.
